assumptions.text: 25% of monthly active users are daily active
3 sessions per active user per day
4x peak factor from EU business-hours concentration

components.name: Application instances
components.justification: 208 peak RPS at 80 ms is 17 in-flight requests; 6 instances at 60% utilisation.

components.name: Background workers
components.justification: 200,000 jobs/day at 0.8 s mean is 2.3 jobs/second; 4 workers at 70% utilisation.

components.name: PostgreSQL primary
components.justification: 21 writes/second is three orders of magnitude inside a single primary's capacity.

components.name: Read replica
components.justification: Isolates reporting queries from the transactional path; 187 peak reads/second.

components.name: Redis
components.justification: Justified by shared state across 6 instances — sessions, per-tenant rate limits, idempotency keys — not by load relief, which would be marginal.

components.name: Observability
components.justification: 99.9% target requires diagnosing incidents within the 43-minute monthly budget.

rejected_components.reason: 21 writes/second and 2.3 jobs/second. A broker solves a throughput problem two orders of magnitude beyond measured demand, and the database-backed queue gives atomicity with the business write for free.
rejected_components.revisit_when: Sustained above 500 events/second, or 3+ independent consumer groups confirmed to need replay of the same stream.

rejected_components.reason: 6 instances at a pool of 5 is 30 connections against a limit of 100 — 30%. Measured mean concurrency is 1.25 queries.
rejected_components.revisit_when: Total connections exceed 80% of max_connections for 1 hour, recurring.

rejected_components.reason: Two deployable types with no dedicated operations capacity. 4 complexity points against a budget with 4 remaining.
rejected_components.revisit_when: More than 4 independently deployable services, and a dedicated platform engineer on the team.

rejected_components.reason: Database full-text search meets the current project and task search requirement.
rejected_components.revisit_when: Search p95 exceeds 300 ms, or ranking requirements exceed what the database provides.

options.description: Single deployable plus workers, managed datastores
trade_offs: Deploys couple the web and worker code paths
Redis is a new datastore technology the team must learn

options.description: As selected but without the read replica
options.reason: Reporting queries would contend with transactional work on the primary. Revisit if reporting moves to a scheduled export.
18 points against a budget of 13, with no dedicated operations capacity. Neither the throughput nor the team structure justifies it.
trade_offs: Independent scaling and deployment per domain

availability.explanation: 43 minutes per month. Multi-AZ database with automated failover, multiple instances behind health checks, rolling deploys, and tested restores reach this. 99.99% would not be achievable: recovery still has manual steps.

triggers.action: Optimise queries before scaling; re-run capacity analysis
Evaluate a connection pooler against measured concurrency
Re-run capacity analysis for the async subsystem; evaluate broker options

triggers.metric: largest tenant share of total load
triggers.action: Evaluate moving the largest tenant to a dedicated database
Review which read paths tolerate this lag

open_questions: Does EU data residency extend to backups and observability data?
Is any single tenant expected to exceed 15% of total load?
